boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented UMBC rituals and recurring community events, from a golden-nosed mascot to a class-free midday block.

cards.title: The scheduled Free Hour
cards.subtitle: UMBC academic calendar, Monday–Wednesday–Friday
cards.notes: Plan a club meeting, campus event, or lunch during the noon-to-1 p.m. class-free block on Monday, Wednesday, or Friday.
cards.short_summary: A student-created class-free hour that remains part of UMBC life.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC’s SGA history says students called for a Monday, Wednesday, and Friday Free Hour with no scheduled classes in 1970, and that it continues to exist.
cards.access_notes: The university’s event-services guidance identifies Free Hour as noon–1 p.m. on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.

cards.title: Rub the Retriever’s golden nose
cards.subtitle: True Grit statue near the Administration Building and RAC
cards.notes: Find the bronze True Grit statue and add a quick nose rub before finals, Convocation, or Commencement for the campus good-luck ritual.
cards.short_summary: Students mark milestones and seek finals luck at the mascot sculpture.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC documents that students and alumni rub the bronze True Grit sculpture’s nose for good luck, including around Convocation, Commencement, and finals.
cards.source_title: How To Be A Retriever! – UMBC
cards.access_notes: The source locates the sculpture on the plaza between the Administration Building and Retriever Athletic Center.

cards.title: Come home in black and gold
cards.subtitle: Annual UMBC Homecoming week
cards.notes: Check the Homecoming calendar for the annual week of reunions, carnival activities, athletics, and Retriever-pride events.
cards.short_summary: A multi-day gathering that has connected the UMBC community since 1976.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC says Homecoming has been an annual multi-day event since 1976; its current site describes annual bonfire, reunions, carnival, and athletic events.
cards.access_notes: The Homecoming site lists the 2026 celebration for the week of October 31; consult its schedule as events are announced.

cards.title: Start Homecoming around the bonfire
cards.subtitle: Erickson Field
cards.notes: Join the Homecoming kickoff on Erickson Field and follow organizer instructions around the professionally managed annual bonfire.
cards.short_summary: A student-originated fire-lighting tradition that has anchored Homecoming since 2004.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC reports that the first Homecoming Bonfire was held in 2004 and that the tradition has continued annually as a Homecoming centerpiece.
cards.source_title: Building the bonfire from scratch – UMBC
cards.access_notes: UMBC’s traditions page identifies Erickson Field as the bonfire location; attend only during the scheduled, staffed event.

cards.title: Close spring with Quadmania
cards.subtitle: Annual spring festival hosted by UMBC’s Student Events Board
cards.notes: Watch for the spring schedule and choose from the outdoor festival, games, music, and Retriever Quest activities offered that year.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC’s Student Events Board identifies Quadmania as its annual spring festival and describes music, an all-day carnival, and Retriever Quest.
cards.source_title: Annual Events – Student Events Board – UMBC
cards.access_notes: Programming changes by year; use the Student Events Board’s current announcements for date and participation details.

cards.title: See Pangea’s cultural showcase
cards.subtitle: Welcome Week cultural student-organization event
cards.notes: During Welcome Week, look for the student-led showcase to watch performances and meet cultural organizations sharing their work.
cards.short_summary: A Welcome Week cultural showcase created by UMBC students.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC says Pangea debuted in fall 2016 after students worked with cultural organizations and staff, and that it became a campus tradition.
cards.source_title: SPACES: Co-Creating Communities at UMBC – UMBC
cards.access_notes: UMBC lists Pangea as a Welcome Week cultural showcase; confirm the current program and location before attending.

cards.title: Sing “Our UMBC” at milestones
cards.subtitle: Convocation and Commencement ceremony tradition
cards.notes: Listen for the alma mater at Convocation or Commencement, and join the singing if you know the words and ceremony guidance permits.
cards.short_summary: A 2006 alma mater sung at UMBC’s major academic ceremonies.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC states that its alma mater debuted in 2006 and is sung at Convocation and Commencement.
cards.source_title: How To Be A Retriever! – UMBC
cards.access_notes: This is part of scheduled university ceremonies; ceremony access and participation guidance can vary.

cards.title: Take a finals break at Midnight Breakfast
cards.subtitle: End-of-semester event at True Grit’s dining hall
cards.notes: During finals season, check Residential Student Association announcements for the late-evening breakfast and stress-break programming at True Grit’s.
cards.short_summary: An end-of-semester gathering that turns the dining hall into a finals break.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC describes Midnight Breakfast as a Residential Student Association tradition held before finals, with breakfast and community activities at True Grit’s.
cards.source_title: How To Be A Retriever! – UMBC
cards.access_notes: The cited UMBC account says the event usually runs 10 p.m.–2 a.m.; confirm the current semester’s time and entry requirements.

cards.title: Make election night a campus event
cards.subtitle: The Commons, during U.S. presidential election cycles
cards.notes: During a presidential-election year, look for campus partners’ program details for the watch party, discussions, games, and civic-engagement activities.
cards.short_summary: A UMBC election-night gathering built around civic engagement and community.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC says its Election Night Extravaganza has created a community space around presidential elections since 2004, with the Center for Democracy and Civic Life and student governments hosting.
cards.source_title: How To Be A Retriever! – UMBC
cards.access_notes: This tradition is tied to U.S. presidential election cycles; follow current UMBC civic-life announcements for details.

cards.title: Cheer the Homecoming Puppy Parade
cards.subtitle: Erickson Field during UMBC Homecoming
cards.notes: At Homecoming, watch costumed dogs and their people parade on Erickson Field; bring a pet only if the current event rules allow it.
cards.short_summary: A dog-centered Homecoming tradition that became annual after returning in 2019.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC says the Puppy Parade began for its 2016 fiftieth birthday and became an annual Homecoming tradition after returning in 2019.
cards.source_title: Celebrate Your Retriever Spirit At Homecoming 2023 – UMBC
cards.access_notes: The cited UMBC coverage places the parade on Erickson Field; consult the current Homecoming schedule and pet-participation rules.
